name: MATTIS
description: Mattis (also known as Skitgubbe in Sweden) is a unique two-phase card game popular in Scandinavia. The first phase involves collecting cards by winning tricks, while the second phase reverses the objective - players try to get rid of their collected cards by beating opponents' cards. The last player holding cards loses. It is a game of strategic timing and card management.

content.text: Mattis (also known as Skitgubbe in Sweden) is a unique two-phase card game popular in Scandinavia. The first phase involves collecting cards by winning tricks, while the second phase reverses the objective - players try to get rid of their collected cards by beating opponents' cards. The last player holding cards loses. It is a game of strategic timing and card management.
The game originated in Finland as Myllymatti (mentioned in 19th century newspaper articles) and spread to Sweden where it became known as Skitgubbe. The Norwegian variant is called Mattis.
3 players (standard). Can be adapted for 2 or 4 with modifications.
Standard 52-card deck. Ranking: A (high), K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 (low).
Three cards each; remainder forms face-down stock. With three players one card remains in the stock or is set aside.

items.text: Myllymatti (Finnish): The original Finnish version with slightly different dealing rules.
Skitgubbe (Swedish): Swedish variant with optional rules for compulsory ties.
Four-Player Mattis: Played with partnerships or each player for themselves with a double deck.
